newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan rebels say they captured strategic town.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say they captured strategic town.

text.p: The Sudan People's Liberation Army, which has recently claimed a string of successes in fighting in southern Sudan, said on Sunday its forces had taken Yirol, a strategic town in the Lakes (Buheyrat) State.

"The capture of Yirol ends any hope of land reinforcements reaching the beleaguered government garrison in Juba, the main town in the south, from Bahr el Gazal region," SPLA spokesman Yasir Arman told Reuters by telephone from Eritrea.

He said the battle in Yirol on Saturday lasted five and a half hours. Many of the 900 to 1,000 troops stationed there were killed, others fled south towards Juba, he said, and the SPLA captured large quantities of arms and ammunition.
At the end of April the SPLA captured Rumbek, the Lakes state capital, 380 km (235 miles) northwest of Juba and 100 km (60 miles) west of Yirol, and later took Tonj, further west.
The SPLA has been fighting the Sudan government since 1983, demanding independence or autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem government in Khartoum.
